headline: Histology and transcriptomics predict spatial protein and multi-omic profiles
label: Spatial Multimodal Omics Inference
summary: Recent preprints and papers infer spatial protein, expression and nuclear morphology from partial inputs, reducing reliance on dense paired measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned translation between spatial measurement layers. QUEST virtually stains H&E histology to predict multiplex immunofluorescence protein expression across cellular and tissue scales, and MorphoProt applies RNA-guided cross-attention over multiscale histology and tissue neighborhoods to predict spatial protein abundance. MAD conditionally edits nucleus images and CosMx SMI kidney gene expression together. At tissue scale, CORAL integrates transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic spatial omics with graph attention, and DIRAC performs vertical multi-omic and cross-study integration with label transfer. PhenoMe is a distinct element, an open-source interactive framework for exploring foundation-model embeddings of microscopy data. The new element across the generative and integrative methods is inference of one measurement layer from another, including from histology alone or RNA-conditioned morphology.
